title: Primary Navigation Interaction Guide
intro: A spec-ready rule set for primary navigation, refined over ten years and written to hand to engineering. Most navigation failures come from hover-driven behaviour and split rows.

learn.title: Two item types, no hybrids
learn.text:
**Destination items** are links with no indicator.
**Menu items** are buttons with an indicator and an expanded/collapsed state.

**No split rows.** A row navigates or opens a menu, never both. If the parent has its own page, put an “Overview” link inside the menu.

try.q: A top-level item both links to a section page and opens a submenu. What does the guide say?
options: Pick one; put an “Overview” link in the menu
Keep both but enlarge the chevron
Make the link work on click and the menu on hover
Allow it only on desktop screens
try.explain: A row navigates or opens a menu, never both.

left.label: Breaks navigation
items: A tiny chevron is the only target

right.label: Calabro's rules
items: Only click, tap, Enter or Space

learn.title: Hover is decoration
learn.text:
Activation is **click, tap, Enter or Space** — never hover.

Hover can't open, close or dismiss anything, change ARIA state, or affect tab order. Moving the pointer away does **not** close an open menu.

Dismissal: re-activate the trigger, click outside, or press Esc — with focus returning to the trigger.

try.q: A user opens a menu, then moves the mouse away. What should happen?
options: The menu closes after a short delay
try.explain: Hover is visual only; it can't dismiss anything.

learn.title: Semantics and targets
learn.text:
Use **native HTML before ARIA**: a landmark for the nav, real buttons and links, and `aria-expanded` on menu triggers.

Don't put `role="menu"` on site navigation — that role is for application menus, and it changes the keyboard model users expect.

Targets are at least **24×24 px** and spaced apart, and focus is visible and clearly distinct from hover.

try.q: Which attribute belongs on a navigation menu trigger?
try.explain: It communicates the expanded or collapsed state; role="menu" is for application menus.

test.q: Which inputs may activate a navigation item?
What is the minimum target size in the guide?
test.explain: And targets must be spaced apart.

test.q: Why avoid role="menu" on site navigation?
options: It sets up an application keyboard model users don't expect
It is deprecated in current ARIA versions

test.q: What happens to focus when a menu is dismissed with Esc?
options: It moves to the first page heading
It moves to the next navigation item
test.explain: Returning focus keeps keyboard users oriented.

test.q: Why did Calabro publish this as a spec?
options: So it can be handed straight to engineering
To replace the W3C navigation guidance
Because his earlier articles were too theoretical
To standardise navigation across design systems
test.explain: It is the document he had refined over ten years of writing similar ones.
